_doc: Host-side Waydroid resource policy (consumed by configuration_containers.nix). The Android workload runs in the LXC container cgroup (top-level lxc.pivot tree), NOT under waydroid-container.service's cgroup — so a systemd CPUQuota/AllowedCPUs on the service does NOT constrain it. The cap must be an LXC cgroup2 directive injected into the generated config (config_base). We use cpu.max (bandwidth) rather than cpuset.cpus (pinning): cpu.max cannot fail container start (no cpuset parent-delegation dependency), and per-period throttling frees ALL cores when the quota is spent, so the desktop is never starved for a whole period.

cgroup._doc: cpu.max = '<quota_us> <period_us>'. quota = cpu_max_cores * cpu_period_us. The SP8 has 8 logical CPUs; capping at 7 leaves >=1 core of headroom so a runaway Android workload can never peg all 8 and freeze the machine.

data_heal._doc: SELF-HEAL for the mutable Waydroid /data (the non-deterministic part of the container — the image is RO/immutable, /data is a rw btrfs subvol that drifts). configuration_waydroid-data-heal.nix runs a oneshot BEFORE each waydroid-container.service start that asserts these ownership invariants. Android runs with NO uid-shift here, so Android uid == host uid. recursive=true detects a wrong owner ANYWHERE under the path (the keystore bug had a correct 1017 dir but 1000-owned *.sqlite files inside) and chowns the whole subtree. Best-effort: failures are logged (journalctl -t waydroid-data-heal), never block the container.

invariants._why: AID_KEYSTORE. If keystore/*.sqlite isn't owned by 1017, keystore2 hits SQLITE_CANTOPEN -> aborts -> system_server dies -> Waydroid forever-load. This is the exact corruption the `chown -R ~/.local` bug caused on every rebuild.
